stories.title: Nasdaq hits new record as global bond yields climb
stories.whats_going_on: Wall Street's tech-heavy Nasdaq reached a fresh record high as a global bond sell-off pushed yields higher. The yield on the US 10-year Treasury touched a fresh 24-year high amid heavy market activity.
stories.what_it_means: Rising bond yields generally mean investors are demanding higher returns for lending money to governments, which can ripple through the wider financial system. At the same time, major equity markets continue to find strong momentum from tech and AI investments.
stories.why_care: For everyday investors, big swings in global bond yields can influence wider borrowing costs and create turbulence in mixed-asset investment funds.

stories.title: Ex-Bank of England chief warns Britain is on thin ice
stories.whats_going_on: A former Bank of England chief economist warned that Britain is on thin ice and must act to appease financial markets. The UK currently faces the highest government borrowing costs in the G7.
stories.what_it_means: When a country's borrowing costs climb, the government faces tighter fiscal pressure to reassure international investors and rating agencies. This economic backdrop feeds directly into domestic debates over public spending and taxes.
stories.why_care: Higher national borrowing costs can eventually filter down into broader economic pressures, potentially influencing everything from mortgage pricing to the wider cost of living.

stories.title: Average UK five-year mortgage rate hits 6%
stories.whats_going_on: The average rate for a new UK five-year fixed mortgage reached 6% for the first time in three years. Lenders have been adjusting their pricing upward as they face persistent funding cost pressures.
stories.what_it_means: Borrowing costs for property buyers have crept steadily higher after a period of relative calm, putting additional pressure on household budgets. For comparison, new mortgages in Portugal average around 3%, while 12-month Euribor sits at 3.247%.
stories.why_care: Anyone coming to the end of a fixed-rate deal or looking to buy a home will face notably higher monthly repayments than they did a few years ago.

stories.title: BT rescues TalkTalk in £400m broadband deal
stories.whats_going_on: BT agreed to buy broadband supplier TalkTalk in a £400 million rescue deal designed to protect 900 jobs and secure 1.5 million customers. Rival broadband providers have raised competition concerns over the tie-up.
stories.what_it_means: Corporate consolidation in the telecoms sector often happens when smaller or heavily indebted players face acute financial strain. Regulators and competitors scrutinise these rescue deals closely to ensure consumer choice isn't harmed.
stories.why_care: For household bill-payers, shifts in the broadband market can eventually influence broadband and phone package pricing as provider landscapes change.

carousel.title: Navigating today's rising UK mortgage rates

slides.t: Borrowing costs are making headlines again. If you are buying a home or nearing the end of a fix, here is what is actually going on.
Lenders are adjusting their pricing upward to manage persistent funding cost pressures across the wider financial markets. It is a bumpy time for the housing sector.

slides.h: What this means for your monthly bills
slides.t: Anyone locking in a new deal now will face notably higher monthly repayments than they did a few years ago. Budgets are feeling the squeeze.
Review your household outgoings early, speak to a whole-of-market broker well before your current deal ends, and give your emergency fund some extra love.
